title: Seedance Video Edit — MiniMax performance with approved Riley references

assistant_visual_review.method: Sampled native video via 24-frame overview and nine-frame 0.125-second catch detail, compared with original full contact sheet and approved face/wardrobe stills; full-frame decode and numeric audio analysis. No real-time playback or independent listening claim.
observations: The actual-video edit follows the preferred MiniMax performance closely in sampled frames: already-airborne mug, frontal-to-side-to-rear camera arc, catch, handback and cyan-wake departure.
Hand and mug make contact around1.75–2.0 seconds in the focused samples; no visible deliberate drop or toss.
Handback spans approximately5.1–6.1 seconds, followed by a cyan-wake exit from about6.4 seconds.
Short brown bob, gold sleeveless mini-dress, black/gold tall boots and mostly human skin with narrow cyan/chrome accents remain recognizable.
Cyan implanted eye and cheek treatment are more conspicuous than in the original source; the picture remains close to the original action and environment.
limitations: Returned185 picture frames at24fps (7.709s), versus192 frames/eight seconds in the source: seven fewer frames, approximately0.292s shorter. Exact source timing was not preserved; the reason for this provider change is unverified. No local retiming applied.

Exact portrait likeness is not established. Face remains narrow/stylized and the detailed asymmetric silver/magenta facial and neck design is simplified; stronger cyan treatment alone is not proof of better identity consistency.
Source slow reach, near-suspended cup and weak sharp lateral eye flick remain. This edit tests appearance refinement, not a new action performance.
Camera is a broad arc, not a verified360-degree circle. Patron geography and frame-to-frame finger contact still need playback review.
Native stereo audio has been decoded and measured only; speech/music absence, event synchronization and subjective continuity have not been independently heard.
